messages:
oncall-bot: PAGING: Sev1 - runtime latency spike + pod crashes in us-west-2 (auto-escalation). Incident channel created. Please ack if you're available.

oncall-bot: Affected service: redwood-serving-runtime. Symptoms: sustained 95th pct token latency > 4s, burst OOMs, pod restarts. Recent deploy? no.

maya: acked. I'm the on-call. grabbing diag now. seeing a cluster of pods in CrashLoopBackOff and kubelet logs show OOM kills.

jonathan: I'm nearby, can help with node-level checks. maya, can you confirm which pod group?

maya: looks like the "dynamic-batcher" replicas on nodepool-runtime-a. pods: runtime-batcher-5fgh, runtime-batcher-9klm, runtime-infer-2abc. kube-events show repeated "OOMKilled" and then "container runtime removed".

li: pulling recent logs from one of the batcher pods:
```
E0315 14:02:10.123 runtime: batch growth exceeded capacity, queue length 32768
E0315 14:02:10.124 runtime: attempt to allocate KV cache page failed, fallback disabled
E0315 14:02:10.126 runtime: cuda error during matmul: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
E0315 14:02:10.127 kernel: process 15233 (batcher) killed by OOM
```

serge: that queue length is wild — suggests the batching aggregator stopped draining but kept accepting requests. Could be deadlock or backpressure misfire.

maya: customers are hitting 500s and lots of retries. Telemetry shows a few enterprise keys with high error rates (acct: acme-inc). Notified success manager.

jonathan: quick mitigation idea: scale down dynamic-batcher to 0 to stop new batching aggregation, then scale up plain infer replicas (stateless) to absorb traffic. We should route by policy to stateless model variant.

ops-bot: runbook suggestion:
- step1: cordon affected nodes
- step2: drain pods gracefully (grace period 60s)
- step3: disable dynamic batching via feature-flag (configmap)
- step4: scale up inferers by +3 replicas

maya: doing step4 first: increasing infer replicas now to reduce latency for new requests.

jonathan: I'll flip the configmap to disable batching after Maya confirms extra capacity is up.

maya: infra change in progress: `kubectl scale deploy redwood-infer --replicas=6 -n runtime` (apply), now checking pod readiness.

li: also seeing kernel OOM logs on node-runtime-3: "Out of memory: Killed process 29821 (gunicorn) total-vm:..." Node-level memory spike aligned with batch growth.

serge: possible root cause: a regression in the batching aggregator where a new request path stops releasing the batch lock on error, causing unbounded accumulation and memory growth. There's an earlier PR that touched the aggregator commit 8f3b2a.

maya: acme-inc is getting 503s, ops is telling them degraded. I opened a support note. SLA risk flagged.

jonathan: configmap flip to disable batching done (commit applied). waiting for batcher pods to reload.

maya: batcher pods are failing fast on restart with the same OOMs — even with batching off, existing containers have huge resident sets. I'm going to force-delete the worst pods to free node memory.

li: command run: `kubectl delete pod runtime-batcher-5fgh -n runtime --grace-period=0 --force`

ops-bot: alert: node-runtime-3 memory pressure. Suggest cordon + drain: `kubectl cordon node-runtime-3 && kubectl drain node-runtime-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

maya: cordoned node-runtime-3 and draining. Observed that two infer pods also moved off.

jonathan: after force-delete, new pods come up with lower RSS. GPU memory freed. CUDA errors no longer appear in fresh pods.

li: sample new log block after restart:
```
I0315 14:13:45.012 runtime: batching disabled via config
I0315 14:13:45.013 runtime: init complete, KV cache size 0
I0315 14:13:45.220 runtime: serving ready
```

maya: latency improving for most routes, 95th down to ~600ms. Still a few tails due to retries.

serge: we need to prevent recurrence. Plan: revert the aggregator PR, add invariant checks on batch lock ownership, and add circuit-breaker to reject requests when queue length > threshold. Also run a memory-pressure fuzz test.

jonathan: agree. I'll open an emergency PR to revert 8f3b2a and add a short-term guardrails patch.

elaine: I'll notify Customer Success and Ops with an incident summary and affected customers list (acme-inc, globex). ETA to full recovery?

maya: marking incident as "mitigated" for now — traffic has fallen back to normal but we're tracking until no restarts for 30m.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> partial recovery. Next update scheduled in 15m.

li: followups: collect full heapdumps from sample batcher process before we delete remaining crash pods, to confirm deadlock path and leaked buffers. Also snapshot node-runtime-3 metrics.

maya: created ticket INF-4432 with logs, heapdumps, and config diffs. Assigning to eng-runtime with priority P0.

jonathan: pushed emergency revert PR #4829 (WIP). running CI.

serge: long-term items: add static limits on aggregator queue, instrument per-tenant queue usage to throttle heavy keys, test rollback scenarios for config flips.

elaine: CS notified, they escalated to acme product lead, provided graded timeline: initial mitigation done, full root cause + postmortem in 48 hours.

maya: final: leaving a note for on-call handoff at 15:00 UTC. jonathan will take the follow-up shift.

jonathan: taking follow-up. thanks all.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: last_message_ts=1815679005, state=mitigated, assigned_followup=jonathan, incident_id=INC-2026-144."
